story.title: India Is Building AI That Understands Its Languages
story.sourceContext: 25 November showcase; official announcement 26 November; developer-reported results
story.claimStage: unveiled; reported evaluation, no independent model benchmark

scenes.headline:
Chariot-1
Homegrown AI
scenes.narration: Chariot Artificial Intelligence, an Indian AI company, has unveiled Chariot One, a family of language and speech models trained from scratch in India.

scenes.headline:
Selective
activation
scenes.narration: Its largest language model contains nearly eleven billion parameters, but selectively activates around four billion for each token it processes.

scenes.headline:
Many scripts.
Shared symbols.
scenes.narration: Its IndicShift technology represents characters from twelve Indian scripts using a shared alphabet, reportedly reducing the number of tokens needed by up to sixty percent.
scenes.note: Normalized reported maximum reduction, not actual measured tokenization

scenes.headline:
Three models.
One training run.
scenes.narration: Another innovation, called Nested Training, allows three differently sized models to be developed through a single training run.

scenes.headline:
From text
to natural speech.
scenes.narration: Chariot's speech model also supports English and at least ten Indian languages, interpreting numbers, abbreviations and measurements in context.

scenes.headline:
AI for a
multilingual India.
scenes.narration: Supported by the IndiaAI Mission, Chariot is helping build AI technology designed around India's own linguistic diversity.
